title: Fixed term employment - rights compared to permanent employees
p1:
A fixed-term employee can have the same workplace benefits as a permanent employee — even though their job has an end date.

Many people assume that a temporary contract automatically means fewer employment rights. That assumption can cost workers money and leave them accepting less than they may legally be entitled to.
p2:
In India, fixed-term employment generally means hiring someone for a specific period under a written employment contract. The job ends when the agreed term expires, unless the contract is renewed or the employment continues under applicable rules.

But here’s the surprising part: fixed-term employees may be entitled to benefits comparable to permanent employees performing similar work, including applicable statutory benefits and proportionate benefits where the law provides for them. The contract’s end date does not automatically erase those rights.
p3:
There is one crucial distinction. A fixed-term employee generally cannot assume that the contract will be renewed, while a permanent employee usually has continuing employment subject to applicable termination rules and conditions.

Before signing, check the contract duration, salary, leave, social security contributions, gratuity eligibility, and termination provisions. Also verify which labour laws and rules apply to your establishment and employment arrangement. The exact entitlement depends on the applicable law and the facts of the case.
conclusion: If two employees perform similar work but one has a fixed-term contract and the other is permanent, which benefits do you think should be identical — and where should the law draw the line?
